transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Jon Reynolds (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Horizon - Procurement), Rahul Mehta (Horizon - Security), Tom Alvarez (Horizon - FinOps), Priya Singh (Horizon - Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be spotty):
- Team discusses pricing tiers, potential volume commitment, and privileged access approach.
- Legal flags a DPA clause around data deletion timelines and audit logs.
- Security requests clarification on KMS/HSM support and key ingress/egress.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aisha Khan: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, uh this should be about an hour, we put a bit more time to go through legal and the technical bits — i'm aisha from redwood.
[00:12] Laura Chen: great, thanks aisha. i wanted to make sure we tackle cost variability up front, tom is here from finance to help with the expected volumes.
[00:20] Tom Alvarez: yeah hi, i'll try not to derail with invoicing minutiae but we do need predictable egress and per-token cost estimates.
[00:28] Jon Reynolds: quick intro, i'm jon, i'll cover the VPC/KMS preflight and the integration surface for privileged keys.
[00:35] Priya Singh: and i'm priya on legal, i want to flag data retention, audit trails and the deletion SLA.
[00:42] Rahul Mehta: and rahul, security — interested in key custody and whether we can use hsm on-prem or managed kms.

[02:10] Aisha Khan: to kick off, quick context — horizon is evaluating redwood for inference endpoints, mixed hosted plus private for regulated flows. today we'll align on MSA/DPA exceptions, privileged keying, and pricing pathing for a pilot.

[04:05] Laura Chen: the procurement question is: do we sign a standard msa or do we need specific exceptions for bank data? we've got previous vendors asking for limited data use clauses.
[04:28] Priya Singh: exact wording — we need clause that says redwood will not retain raw customer prompts beyond X days and will surface audit logs for any privileged access within 7 days. also TLS is baseline. there may be an exception around telemetry.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: understood — our standard dpa allows retention windows configurable per-customer, we can set to 30 days by default and add a manual deletion SLA, but priya can you say what horizon's target is?
[05:36] Priya Singh: ideally 7 days for non-PII, and immediate deletion for PII on request; financial transactions need additional controls for 90-day audit retention. it's a mix, so we need a matrix.

[07:45] Jon Reynolds: from the technical side, for privileged keys we support both cloud KMS integrations and bring-your-own-key models. HSM-backed keys (via partner HSM) is possible but requires additional provisioning and a different billing path.
[08:12] Rahul Mehta: can you clarify "bring-your-own-key" — does the data ever leave horizon's key domain? we need assurances keys never leave and that redwood cannot export them.
[08:30] Jon Reynolds: good question — our BYOK integrates with customer KMS via standard envelope encryption; redwood services can use the keys for encryption/decryption in memory but we do not export key material. for HSM, the operations can be scoped to the customer's HSM via remote attestation in some setups. i'll follow up with docs.

[10:50] Tom Alvarez: how does that affect cost? if we require HSM-backed flows for all enterprise traffic, is there a premium?
[11:05] Aisha Khan: yes, usually HSM has a cost delta — plus integration/setup. for pricing we typically separate hosted tokens vs private/dedicated pool tokens and add a privileged-key surcharge if HSM required.

[13:20] Laura Chen: okay, procurement needs a banded pricing model: list price, committed tier price (for pilot), and an overage policy. also we need to see a sample invoice.
[13:40] Aisha Khan: we'll put together a pilot rate card: expected QPS, monthly token forecast, and committed discount tiers. jon will help size the dedicated pool.

[15:55] Rahul Mehta: on SLA — we want 99.9% uptime SLA for critical endpoints and clear incident report timelines. also we need a rollback/failover plan if model variants fail for a critical workflow.
[16:25] Jon Reynolds: redwood supports regional fallback, and can route to a lower-cost model variant automatically. for rollback, we can do canary rollouts and immediate failover to the last-known-good model version. those are part of the Dedicated playbook.

[18:40] Priya Singh: legal will be looking at indemnity and limitation of liability — typical bank exceptions include regulatory fines and data breach caps. are those negotiable?
[19:02] Aisha Khan: we have standard language but enterprise exceptions are possible; we'll need legal to provide the exact wording they require and then our counsel can respond. i've seen a handful of redlines around liability caps at large banks.

[21:10] Tom Alvarez: billing question — do you support committed monthly minimums with true-up? and is there an escrow option for data if we ever offboard?
[21:30] Aisha Khan: yes, committed capacity is supported via Redwood Dedicated with monthly or annual terms and true-up reporting. data escrow is typically handled via DPA addendum — we'll surface the options.

[23:00] Laura Chen: on the onboarding timeline, procurement prefers a 6–8 week contracting window. can we hit that if legal back-and-forth is minimal?
[23:22] Aisha Khan: typically yes, assuming no major redlines. we'll attach a milestone plan to the MSA: signature -> technical preflight -> pilot start.

[25:10] Jon Reynolds: technical preflight checklist highlights: VPC peering, IP allowlists, KMS key policy docs, egress rules, test models and load profile. i'll send a checklist after this call.

[27:50] Rahul Mehta: specific security ask — we need audit trail granularity showing which user/role invoked which model and what prompt was sent, at a minimum for privileged workflows. is that captured?
[28:15] Jon Reynolds: we log request metadata, and we can enable structured audit logs per route with user identity mapped if you provide an auth token mapping. prompts are redacted by default in logs, but for privileged workflows we can provide more detailed logging under contractual agreement.

[30:10] Priya Singh: that sounds promising, but we need to put explicit controls in the DPA about who can request prompt-level logs and under what legal basis.
[30:28] Aisha Khan: fair, we'll note that as a DPA matrix item — who, why, retention, and access process.

[32:45] Tom Alvarez: back to pricing, please include examples: pilot at 20M tokens/month vs projected at 200M tokens/month and how pricing scales. we need that sensitivity analysis for finance.
[33:05] Aisha Khan: we'll prepare three scenarios and include committed-discount breakpoints and HSM surcharges.

[35:40] Laura Chen: procurement needs a single point of contact on the redwood side for contracting and technical handoffs. who is it?
[35:55] Aisha Khan: i'll be AE lead and jon will be SE lead; i'll own contracting. i'll also copy our legal lead when we send the redlines.

[37:10] Rahul Mehta: one more technical: do you have certifications (soc2 type 2 etc) and an options pack for penetration testing evidence?
[37:30] Aisha Khan: yes, soc2 type 2 is available; we can provide an attestation and a pen test summary. for deeper audits we can coordinate an on-site or a third-party scan at cost.

[39:50] Priya Singh: can we model the deletion workflow — we want a 48-hour SLA for deletion of non-essential logs after a request. is that something you can commit to?
[40:10] Jon Reynolds: our deletion pipeline can be configured; 48 hours is aggressive but feasible for certain artifacts. i'll need to map which artifacts (raw prompts, logs, telemetry) and note caveats for backups and third-party storage.

[42:20] Tom Alvarez: fiscal ops question — for committed capacity, is there a split billing option (e.g., commit seat-level vs token-level) and a way to allocate costs to internal teams?
[42:40] Aisha Khan: we have per-token and per-dedicated-pool billing and can support sub-accounting via routes and API keys so you can attribute costs per team. our console exposes token-level cost breakdown.

[45:05] Laura Chen: outstanding blocker is an approved MSA template. procurement needs the redline first, then legal will iterate.
[45:20] Aisha Khan: we'll prioritize sending redlines within 3 business days.

[47:30] Jon Reynolds: i'll also produce a VPC/KMS technical appendix with sample IAM policies and network diagrams.

[49:05] Rahul Mehta: thanks, please include the specific cipher suites and whether mutual TLS is supported end to end.
[49:20] Jon Reynolds: noted, mutual TLS is supported for private deployments and we'll include config steps.

[51:10] Priya Singh: timeline check — once we get redlines, legal will aim for a one-week turnaround if changes are minor; procurement will coordinate internal approvals.

[52:40] Tom Alvarez: i'll try to supply the token forecast and QPS by monday.

[54:00] Aisha Khan: recap — actions: aisha send redlines + SOC2, jon send technical appendix + preflight checklist, rahul confirm HSM requirement, tom send forecast. we'll schedule a pilot-costing readout the week of 2026-01-26. any final questions?
[54:25] Laura Chen: no, thank you all.
[54:30] Priya Singh: thanks, appreciate the notes.
[56:10] Aisha Khan: great — we'll follow up by email, meeting adjourned.
